data.body:
EPIC PLAN REVIEW #5 -> BLOCK, 1 blocking. Pass-4's deleted-key blocker RESOLVED.
BLOCKER (COH,E1): another self-inflicted contradiction — my AC said 'exactly one dict literal across the WHOLE ENGINE' while the Approach explicitly DEFERS config.py's third copy to fe15. An implementer satisfying the Approach fails the AC and vice versa. Narrowed both the epic AC and J2's AC to 'within adapters/' with the grep scoped to src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/, and named config.py:37 as the one knowingly-remaining literal outside that scope.
Also applied the substantive pass-5 advisories:
 - ADV1 (T5c, impact 1.0): the plan required https but said NOTHING about certificate verification — self-hosted DC commonly uses self-signed/internal-CA certs, and disabling verify would make the https requirement theatre. Declared: verification stays ON, never verify=False; internal CAs are handled via a ca_bundle key / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; allow_insecure governs the URL SCHEME ONLY and does not relax cert checking. Added J6 ACs asserting the client is built without verify=False and that allow_insecure does not affect verification.
 - ADV3 (T5e, impact 1.0): I had parameterized the probe's resolved-status set but never said where an operator SETS it. Added reconciler.resolved_statuses (list of workflow state names), defaulting to {Resolved,Done,Cancelled} so conventional workflows configure nothing; Cloud keeps its own frozenset and is not made configurable.
 - ADV4/ADV5 (G3,G4): the epic scope listed _config_schema.py as one atomic item but no child owned the TLS validator. Split explicitly: J6 owns the TLS/allow_insecure validator + ca_bundle + resolved_statuses (lands with the transport that consumes them); J7 owns only the reconciler.backend choice widening.
 - ADV10 (T3): VERIFIED against .github/workflows/_optionality.yml:108 — the clean-core-wheel check lists only langchain/langgraph/anthropic/inspect_ai/opentelemetry, so the epic's 'no new dependency' AC had NO CI teeth. Added 'jira' to that list as a J7 AC.
 - ADV6 (G6): the import-contract mechanism was 'import-linter OR an equivalent grep' — ambiguous, so an implementer would have to decide. CHOSE one: an AST-walking test under tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/, because it runs inside the make test that CI's Verified gate already executes (no new CI job, no new dev dep) and it MATCHES EXISTING REPO PRACTICE — verified test_backend_neutrality.py already does ast.parse + ast.ImportFrom walks at lines 25/107/110. import-linter allowed only if wired into make lint, since a config no target runs is not enforcement.
 - ADV8 (F1): split the bundled runtime-behavior + docs-content AC into two.
 - ADV9 (E1): folded two near-duplicate 'no jira in base install' ACs into the one that now carries CI teeth.
Deferred: ADV2 (restates the blocker I just fixed), ADV7 (P6 generic AC-quality, no specific defect named).
